source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
finding: Large over-generate-then-rank pipeline (generate, dedupe, rank) produced ideas that expert reviewers rated more novel than human expert ideas, with no gain in feasibility.
numbers: Blind review, 49 ideas per condition. Novelty (1-10, per review): human 4.84, AI 5.64 (p<0.01), AI plus human rerank 5.81. Excitement 4.55 vs 5.19 vs 5.46. Feasibility 6.61 vs 6.34 vs 6.44 (n.s.). Overall 4.68 vs 4.85 (n.s.) vs 5.34 (p<0.05). 119 human and 109 AI reviews.
limits: Ideas judged on written proposals, NLP prompting topics. Reviewer agreement is low (56.1% balanced accuracy).
agent_relevance: A real generate-wide then explore/select loop with measured novelty and usefulness. Wide generation raises novelty cheaply; the selector decides whether it helps overall.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
finding: Over-generation saturates: most seed ideas are near-duplicates. The generator, not the filter, is the bottleneck.
numbers: Of 4000 seeds per topic, only about 200 were non-duplicate (cosine sim over 0.8, MiniLM). About 5% remained after dedupe. The share of new non-duplicates falls with every batch and the cumulative count plateaus.
limits: One model family (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), 7 topics, embedding threshold chosen by hand.
agent_relevance: Set generate budget by a duplicate-rate stop rule, not a fixed N. Force diversity (anti-repeat context, different seeds) before adding volume.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
finding: LLMs are poor judges in the explore/select step: every LLM evaluator tested agreed with experts less than experts agreed with each other.
numbers: Balanced accuracy on top/bottom 25% of ideas: human-human 56.1%; Claude-3.5 pairwise ranker 53.3%; Claude direct 51.7%; GPT-4o direct 50.0%; GPT-4o pairwise 45.0%; AI Scientist reviewer 43.3%. Chance is 50%.
limits: Ground truth is itself noisy; ideas are text proposals.
agent_relevance: Self-evaluation as the explore phase is weak for open ideas. Prefer execution (code run, test) over LLM opinion where an executable check exists.

source: Si et al. (2025) The Ideation-Execution Gap
finding: When 43 expert researchers actually executed ideas (over 100 hours each), LLM ideas lost more score than human ideas on novelty, excitement, effectiveness and overall; rankings flipped on many metrics.
numbers: 43 researchers, each executing one randomly assigned idea; drops significant at p<0.05. Exact magnitudes not on the abstract page I read.
quote: human ideas score higher than LLM ideas
limits: Only the abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Supports checking by running things: text-level novelty judged before execution overstates real value. Real exploration must include execution.

source: Tian et al. (2024) MacGyver: Are LLMs Creative Problem Solvers?
finding: Object-repurposing problems (close cousin of Finke parts-to-object): LLMs propose many solutions but often physically infeasible; humans are stronger on feasibility.
numbers: 1,683 problems (1,306 solvable). On 323 problems, % correct: Llama2-7b 35.5, PaLM2 40.6, GPT-3.5 40.6, Claude2 52.7, GPT-4 62.4, humans 65.1. Over several tries GPT-4 63.0 vs human 67.8; best-of-tries 92.3 vs 98.8. Zero-shot GPT-4: 37.5% infeasible, 18.9% efficient.
limits: Humans were non-expert crowdworkers scored by the same rubric.
agent_relevance: Parts-to-object style tasks are where explore (feasibility check) matters more than generate. Wrong-tool use was 42.4% of GPT-4 failures.

source: Tian et al. (2024) MacGyver, prompting scaffolds
finding: Two scaffolds mirrored generate/explore: self-reflection (check feasibility) cut infeasible answers; divergent-then-convergent prompting (generate wide, then pick) raised efficient answers. They help different things.
numbers: GPT-4 on 180 solvable problems: self-reflection cut infeasible solutions by 9.7% (div-conv 4.3%); div-conv raised efficient solutions by 6.5% (self-reflection 2.2%). Self-reflection did not help Claude2 or Llama2-13b; div-conv helped all models.
limits: Gains are single digits; run counts not clear.
agent_relevance: Use a separate diverge step and a separate feasibility-check step as two operators. Do not rely on one prompt to do both.

source: Tian et al. (2024) MacGyver, failure analysis
finding: What the explore phase must catch: most GPT-4 failures were wrong use of a tool, not lack of ideas.
numbers: 200 infeasible GPT-4 solutions: wrong tool usage 42.4%, goal not achieved 17.7%, unavailable tools 16.9%, wrong spatial understanding 10.8%, ignored constraints 9.5%. Hallucination-linked share 26.4%.
limits: Categories hand-coded by the authors.
agent_relevance: A checklist for the explore step: are all parts available, is each used as it physically can be, is every constraint met, does the goal hold.

source: Lu et al. (2025) Benchmarking Language Model Creativity: A Case Study on Code Generation (NeoCoder, Denial Prompting)
finding: Denial prompting adds a hard constraint that bans the technique just used (like Finke's constrained invention). Correct output falls fast while new-technique output rises.
numbers: GPT-4 on Codeforces: pass@1 16.1% at 0 constraints, then 11.6, 7.1, 5.2, 2.3, 2.1% at 5. Constraint following 100% to 14.4%. Divergent creativity 4.5% to 15.3%. Convergent creativity 16.2% to 0.0%. Combined NeoGauge 1.0 at state 0, 1.4 at state 1, 0.0 at states 4 and 5.
limits: Code domain; novelty means technique set differs from human solutions; one best model.
agent_relevance: Constraint raises novelty and wrecks correctness at once. Use one or two bans, verify by running tests, stop when the verifier fails.

source: Lu et al. (2025) Benchmarking Language Model Creativity: A Case Study on Code Generation (NeoCoder, Denial Prompting)
finding: Standard reasoning scaffolds did not raise creativity: MCTS, self-correction, planning and sampling each traded divergent for convergent gains.
numbers: Differences in percentage points were small: planning divergent -1.2 at state 0; self-correction convergent up to 2.5 but divergent near zero or negative; MCTS convergent up to 10.6 with small divergent change. None improved both; NeoGauge change limited.
limits: Four strategies built for code correctness, not novelty.
agent_relevance: A better reasoning loop does not give better ideas. Novelty needs its own operator and its own measure.

source: Padmakumar et al. (2025) Measuring LLM Novelty as the Frontier of Original and High-Quality Output
finding: Novelty = harmonic mean of unseen n-grams and judged quality. Scale and post-training raise novelty through quality; asking for novelty has little effect and often buys originality at the cost of quality.
numbers: OLMo, OLMo-2, Pythia on story, poetry and creative tool use (MacGyver set). Quality scored 0-5 by o3-mini, normalized. Gains plateau from OLMo-2 7B to 32B. Higher temperature first lifts novelty, then quality loss wins.
limits: Open-data models only; LLM judge for quality; n-gram originality is surface level.
agent_relevance: Asking the model to be novel is a weak lever. Wide sampling plus a quality gate is the stronger lever.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) NoveltyBench: Evaluating Language Models for Humanlike Diversity
finding: Models give few distinct answers to the same open prompt; larger models in a family are less diverse. In-context regeneration (show earlier answers, ask for new) works best.
numbers: Distinct answers in 10 samples at temperature 1: Claude-3.5 Sonnet 1.76, gpt-4o 2.88, gemini-2.0-pro 2.25, Llama-3.1-405B 3.20 vs Llama-3.2-1B 6.74; gemma-2-2b 5.66 vs gemma-2-27b 3.03. Paraphrasing and system prompts only marginal. NB-Curated: 100 prompts with 8 human answers each; NB-WildChat 1,000 prompts.
limits: Equivalence classifier only 71-79% accurate; text gives no numbers for strategy gains.
agent_relevance: Stateful generation (each new try sees earlier tries and must differ) is the cheap fix for sameness.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind
finding: Open-ended outputs collapse inside one model and across models; repeated sampling does not find different ideas.
numbers: Infinity-Chat: 26,070 open queries, 31,250 human labels (25 per item), 70+ models. One model, 50 samples at top-p 0.9 temp 1.0: 79% of queries have mean pairwise similarity over 0.8. Across models 71-82% similar. Reward models and LLM judges align worse with humans where raters disagree.
limits: Embedding similarity (text-embedding-3-small) is a proxy.
agent_relevance: Best-of-N from one model is not diverse generation. For open mode, mix distinct seeds, contexts or constraints; judges are weakest where taste differs.

source: Meincke, Mollick, Terwiesch (2024) Prompting Diverse Ideas: Increasing AI Idea Variance
finding: 35 prompts compared on idea diversity for consumer-product ideas. Chain-of-thought (list 100 ideas, then modify each to be bolder) gave the most diverse pool, close to student groups.
numbers: Mean cosine similarity: baseline 0.377, Steve Jobs persona 0.368, HBR creativity tools 0.387; student groups lowest. Unique-idea pool estimate 3,700 (base) vs 4,700 (CoT); repeats 13.8% vs 11.7%. About 15% of CoT runs skipped step 2.
limits: GPT-4 only, one product domain, cosine proxy. Persona gain is tiny (0.009).
agent_relevance: Two steps (many rough ideas, then transform each) is Geneplore generate then transform. It beat persona prompts.

source: Meincke, Mollick, Terwiesch (2024) Prompting Diverse Ideas, exhaustion
finding: Every strategy exhausts its idea pool; the best strategy only delays it.
numbers: About 1,200 ideas per strategy: CoT advantage detectable up to about 750 ideas, strongest between 100 and 500, gone after 750-800.
limits: Pool size depends on the 0.8 cosine threshold.
agent_relevance: Add a stop rule: when new ideas are mostly near-copies, stop generating and change seeds or constraints.

source: Gu et al. (2025) LLMs Can Realize Combinatorial Creativity
finding: A pipeline that retrieves cross-domain concepts at several abstraction levels and recombines components (Boden combinatorial creativity) beat baselines at matching real later research.
numbers: Similarity to real follow-up papers up 7%-10% across metrics on OAG-Bench.
limits: Value judged by similarity to published work, not by testing; preprint.
agent_relevance: Generation seeded by distant retrieved parts is a workable parts-to-object task for ideas. Judge with outside evidence when possible.

source: Gu et al. (2025) combinatorial creativity, framing
finding: Authors note most LLM ideation work tracks only novelty and ignores value, and that LLMs match experts in novelty but lag in usefulness and feasibility.
numbers: Cites Si et al. (2024); no new numbers.
limits: Framing paragraph, not an experiment.
agent_relevance: Report both novelty and usefulness in any test of the schema.

source: LLM as a Designer of Novel Neural Architectures (2026)
finding: Closed generate-evaluate-select-finetune loop with an explicit novelty filter: removing the filter halves distinct outputs.
numbers: DeepSeek-Coder-7B with LoRA, 22 cycles, 50 candidates in cycle 1. Valid rate 44.0% to peak 74.5%. Models at 40% or better accuracy: 2.04% to 92.86%. CIFAR-10 ablation: full 455 novel models; no novelty filter 220; no accuracy threshold 470 but only 34.0% above threshold; no iteration 1 novel model. Filter: 10-gram MinHash, Jaccard 0.90.
limits: One-epoch proxy score; text-level novelty; no repeated runs; gains plateau after about cycle 18.
agent_relevance: Both gates needed: a novelty gate and a validity gate with a verifier that runs. Shingle novelty can be fooled by rewording.

source: Romera-Paredes et al. (2024) Mathematical discoveries from program search with LLMs (FunSearch)
finding: Frozen LLM proposes programs, an evaluator scores them, a database of good programs (islands) feeds back into prompts. A generate-explore loop that found new mathematical results.
numbers: About 1 million LLM samples, 15 samplers, 150 evaluators. Cap set n=8: 512-element set found in only 4 of 140 experiments. Capacity lower bound 2.2180 to 2.2184 (later 2.2202). Bin packing OR1: 5.30% excess vs 5.81% best-fit. Prompts hold k=2 programs.
limits: Needs a cheap exact scorer; no no-LLM baseline in the main text; low hit rate per run.
agent_relevance: Best machine example of Geneplore at scale: wide cheap generation, hard verifier, archive, islands for diversity. Copy the shape on small tasks that have an executable check.

source: Prompt2Craft: Generating Functional Craft Assemblies with LLMs (2025)
finding: Closest machine version of Finke's parts-to-object task: an LLM assembles functional objects from a given parts list; physics simulation is the explore step. Fresh resample beat feedback repair.
numbers: o4-mini (high effort), 8 object classes, 800 images, 41 part types. Success: first try 63.4%; re-prompt without feedback 85.0%; with feedback after collision check 75.7%; plus simulation 77.1%. First-try errors: 200 position/collision, 58 format, 35 physics. Collisions about 69% of errors.
limits: Functions are narrow (hit, support, roll); success is a physical test, not novelty.
agent_relevance: Resampling from scratch beat repairing a flawed draft, since the model anchors on its invalid design. Keep preinventive drafts cheap and throwaway.

source: Chakrabarty et al. (2024) Art or Artifice? LLMs and the False Promise of Creativity
finding: Experts using a Torrance-style rubric (14 binary tests: fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration) found LLM stories passed far fewer tests than professional ones; LLM judges did not match experts.
numbers: 48 stories, 10 expert raters. LLM stories passed 3-10 times fewer tests; GPT-3.5 under 10%, GPT-4 and Claude v1.3 near 30%; professional stories about 84.7%. No LLM assessor correlated positively with experts.
limits: Story writing only; 2023 models.
agent_relevance: Do not trust LLM self-grading of creativity. Use code checks or fixed rubrics with spot checks.

source: Atmakuru et al. (2024) CS4: Measuring Creativity of LLMs by Controlling the Number of Story-Writing Constraints
finding: More constraints lower the chance of retelling a memorized story, so constraint count probes creativity; satisfaction falls as constraints grow, at different speeds per model.
numbers: 7 to 39 constraints: satisfaction drop about 35% for LLaMA-2 7B vs about 20% for Gemma-7B. At 7 to 23 constraints LLaMA-2 stays coherent but satisfies 25% fewer. Preference tuning helps pick better stories from training data, not make unseen ones.
limits: GPT-4 as judge; story domain.
agent_relevance: Constraints trade instruction-following for novelty. Keep constraint count small and always check satisfaction.

source: Ismayilzada, Beaty et al. (2026) LLMs Align with the Human Brain during Creative Thinking
finding: Alternate Uses Task: bigger and better-scoring LLMs have prompt-stage representations closer to human default-mode-network activity. Not a prompting study.
numbers: 24 models; prompt-stage DMN alignment vs model size r=0.55 (Bonferroni p=0.016), vs AUT score r=0.52 (p=0.036). Human fMRI from 170 participants, 46 stimuli. Control tasks showed no effect. A reasoning-distilled Llama shows negative alignment with high-creativity responses; not replicated in Qwen.
limits: Correlational; no creativity prompting tested.
agent_relevance: Weak hint that reasoning-heavy post-training may cost divergent ability (hypothesis only).

source: Bellemare-Pepin et al. (2025) Divergent Creativity in Humans and Large Language Models
finding: On the Divergent Association Task some LLMs beat average humans, but the most creative humans still beat the best models.
numbers: Human sample 100,000. Model scores are not on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract page only; DAT measures word distance, not useful invention.
agent_relevance: Word-distance divergence is easy to reach; usefulness is untested. Do not use DAT as our metric.

source: Naeini et al. (2023) Large Language Models are Fixated by Red Herrings (Only Connect Wall)
finding: On a group-and-connect puzzle with built-in red herrings, GPT-4 stays far below humans; removing herrings lifts accuracy sharply, so the failure is fixation. More examples did not help.
numbers: 494 test walls. Walls solved: GPT-4 5-7, best embeddings 1, humans 285. Correct groups: GPT-4 269-272 vs humans 1,405 of 1,976. WordNet set without herrings: GPT-4 0-shot solved 471. Shuffled set: 59. One to ten shots gave no consistent gain.
limits: Chain-of-thought not tested. Link to fixation subfield.
agent_relevance: Cross-link to fixation: the first reading dominates; a generate step must force different readings.

source: EscapeBench (2024) Towards Advancing Creative Intelligence of Language Model Agents
finding: Room-escape agent tasks need creating and combining tools. A scaffold of Foresight (propose and test tool-use hypotheses) plus Reflection (task list of open and failed attempts) cut hints about half.
numbers: 36 settings. Humans need 4.33 hints, 257.8 steps, 59.65% early-exit progress. GPT-4o base: 10.30 hints, 723.6 steps, 24.75%. With EscapeAgent: 5.03 hints, 452.8 steps, 47.03%. GPT-4o-mini 15.19 to 10.58 hints. Ablation: Reflection alone beat Foresight alone; both best (9.83 to 5.00 hints).
limits: Still about 2x human steps; large models gather tools but rarely try creative actions.
agent_relevance: An agent loop close to generate-explore: hypothesis before action plus memory of failures. Reuse in S3/S4.

source: Creative Problem Solving in Large Language and Vision Models: What Would it Take? (2024)
finding: Argues search only in output space is not enough; need to change the conceptual space (Boden exploratory vs transformational). In a small object-replacement test, affordance info in the prompt helped, task info alone hurt.
numbers: 50 samples per model (10 sets, 4 objects). Nominal accuracy CLIP-B-32 100%, ViLT-B-32 68%; random about 30% on replacement. Replacement scores only in plots.
limits: Position paper with a small test.
agent_relevance: Giving the part list with what each part affords beats giving only the goal; fits parts-to-object logic.

source: Absence check: LLM tests of the Finke parts-to-object task
finding: No published study found that runs the Finke, Ward and Smith mental-synthesis (parts-to-object) task on language models, and no implemented Geneplore system.
numbers: Several queries (Geneplore, preinventive, parts-to-object, mental synthesis, language model) gave zero direct hits.
limits: Negative result from search tools, not proof. CREA (arXiv 2504.05306) and a PMC 'System 3' paper (PMC12568592) mention Geneplore in passing; not opened.
agent_relevance: Running parts-to-object on an LLM would be new: random parts, forced category, score originality and practicality, compare plain vs two-phase.
